summary: Stage-only refinement of the eight accepted GS3 fusion targets, retaining their identifiers and importing GS0–GS2. The contracts specify proper-convolution extension, parity-corrected symmetry, arbitrary finite-set collision coherence, continuous product-Weil realization, symmetric constant terms and Verdier duality. All targets are planned; missing formal carriers and the exact Drinfeld coefficient transport are explicit gaps, so the stage is not closed. No geometric theorem is claimed implemented.

nodes.title: Disjoint-leg locus
nodes.statement: For a finite set I partitioned by b:I→K, define U_b ⊂ (Div¹_X)^I by x_i ≠ x_j whenever b(i) ≠ b(j). It allows coincidences inside one block. Pull the existing local Hecke stack and Satake category back to U_b; denote restriction by j_b*. On U_b, completion along the union of block divisors is the product of the block completions, giving the factorization of Grassmannians and local Hecke stacks.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q of characteristic p; G/E is connected reductive.
Λ is a commutative torsion coefficient ring killed by an integer prime to p. The ℓ-adic extension uses a fixed prime ℓ ≠ p and compatible reductions through the imported coefficient adapter.
Satake objects have bounded support, are universally locally acyclic over the leg base, and are flat perverse; representation objects have finite projective coefficient modules.
proofSteps: Use the divisor product equation and invertibility of distinct divisor ideals to split the completed rings, then the loop quotient and torsor descriptions.
An ordered partition gives the same open independently of its ordering; this construction commutes with base change.
acceptance: One block gives the whole leg base.
Singleton blocks exclude every collision, while a two-element block allows its internal diagonal.

sources.match: Exact defining condition of the blockwise disjoint locus and factorization.

nodes.title: Restriction across collision diagonals
nodes.statement: For the blockwise disjoint inclusion j_b, restriction j_b*:Sat^I_G(Λ)→Sat_G(U_b,Λ) is fully faithful, and so is restriction of finite projective local systems on the leg base. Every Satake object satisfies A ≅ pH⁰(Rj_b*j_b*A). This is uniqueness and reconstruction for objects already extending; full faithfulness alone asserts no essential surjectivity.

Λ is a commutative torsion coefficient ring killed by an integer prime to p. The ℓ-adic extension uses a fixed prime ℓ ≠ p and compatible reductions through the imported coefficient adapter.

proofSteps: Filter the complement by smooth partial diagonals of positive ℓ-codimension. Purity makes their i*i! on locally constant perfect complexes lie in degrees ≥2.
The conservatively detecting, t-exact constant-term functors reduce the required perverse bound to that local-system bound.
Apply the open–closed triangle and perverse truncation to obtain the reconstruction and Hom isomorphisms.
acceptance: For two legs the diagonal has codimension one and contributes starting in degree two.
A codimension-zero closed component would invalidate the argument; arbitrary restrictions of arbitrary categories are not fully faithful.

sources.match: Proves the two full-faithfulness assertions by partial diagonal bounds; reconstruction follows in the proof.

nodes.title: Satake support parity
nodes.statement: The parity of a Schubert tuple μ• is ε(μ•)=Σ_i⟨2ρ,μ_i⟩ mod 2 in Z/2. Differences along dominance are sums of coroots, whose pairing with 2ρ is even, so parity is constant on a connected-component stratum and defines an open-and-closed even/odd decomposition of the local Hecke stack. For mixed-parity objects use their canonical summands. The correction scalar for homogeneous A,B is (-1)^{ε(A)ε(B)}.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q of characteristic p; G/E is connected reductive.
Λ is a commutative torsion coefficient ring killed by an integer prime to p. The ℓ-adic extension uses a fixed prime ℓ ≠ p and compatible reductions through the imported coefficient adapter.
Satake objects have bounded support, are universally locally acyclic over the leg base, and are flat perverse; representation objects have finite projective coefficient modules.
proofSteps: Use ⟨2ρ,α∨⟩=2 for each simple coroot and dominance differences to prove constancy on closure relations.
Disjoint unions add dimensions and hence add parity. Apply the sign separately to the four pairs of canonical summands.
acceptance: An odd-dimensional minuscule Schubert object is odd even when its ungraded fibre has even rank.
Parity is additive; an odd/odd swap has scalar -1.

sources.match: The parity decomposition and exact commutativity correction.

The same component parity corrects the alternating Frobenius trace of a perverse shift.

nodes.title: Fusion product and ordinary symmetry
nodes.statement: For blocks I=⊔_a I_a and A_a∈Sat^{I_a}_G(Λ), use the chain of modifications E_0→⋯→E_k, projections p_a to the a-th modification and composition m. Define the fusion object *_{a}A_a=Rm_*(⊗_a p_a*A_a). The construction is ULA, bounded and flat perverse and restricts to ⊠_a A_a on U_b. It is independent of the order by full faithfulness. Apply the fold map I ⊔ I → I (diagonal pullback and the Grassmannian pushforward) to obtain the internal tensor on Sat^I. Modify its geometric commutativity by (-1)^{ε(A)ε(B)}. This gives a symmetric monoidal structure refining the existing convolution, with total cohomology F^I strong symmetric monoidal into ordinary, ungraded finite-projective local systems (with Weil realization in the next target).
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q of characteristic p; G/E is connected reductive.
Λ is a commutative torsion coefficient ring killed by an integer prime to p. The ℓ-adic extension uses a fixed prime ℓ ≠ p and compatible reductions through the imported coefficient adapter.
Satake objects have bounded support, are universally locally acyclic over the leg base, and are flat perverse; representation objects have finite projective coefficient modules.
proofSteps: Construct the proper chain-composition correspondence, whose restriction to disjoint blocks is an isomorphism. ULA stability comes from the IV.2 correspondence criterion.

Apply constant terms: their total pushforward is locally constant perfect and agrees on the disjoint locus with the degree-zero finite-projective exterior product. Density and VI.7.7 imply flat perversity.
Use VI.9.3 for uniqueness of associativity, commutativity and unit comparisons; all relations hold after disjoint restriction.
Total cohomology carries the geometric flip to the graded Koszul flip. The component correction cancels that sign and preserves hexagon, involution and unit laws.
acceptance: For one block recover A itself, and tensor with the zero-modification unit is the original object.
Odd/odd braiding is the negative of the geometric flip; after F it is the ordinary flip.
The construction uses neither rational decomposition nor rational reductivity.
Both hexagons, the pentagon, triangle, double-braiding identity and monoidal interchange commute as diagrams of natural transformations; equality of object isomorphism classes is insufficient.

sources.locator: Proposition VI.9.4 pp228–229; parity convention p228; VI.8.1–VI.8.2 pp224–226
sources.match: Proper chain convolution gives existence of the exterior-product extension; disjoint restriction gives its unique coherent comparisons. Corrected symmetry refines already monoidal convolution.

Coherent multi-leg tensor symmetry supplies representations with colliding labels, without semisimplicity.

nodes.title: CoCartesian finite-set functoriality
nodes.statement: For a map α:I→J, let Δ_α:(Div¹)^J→(Div¹)^I repeat the j-th divisor on its inverse-image block. Pull back along Gr^I_G ×_(Div¹)^I (Div¹)^J → Gr^I_G and push forward along the natural closed immersion Gr^I_G ×_(Div¹)^I (Div¹)^J ↪ Gr^J_G. Descending the required loop equivariance defines α_!:Sat^I→Sat^J; the closed immersion is on Grassmannians, not on quotient Hecke stacks. This merges each fibre of α and inserts unit modifications at empty fibres. For permutations it relabels legs, and for disjoint unions it respects exterior fusion. Canonical identity and composition comparisons satisfy the finite-set coherence relations. Together with exterior fusion they give the coCartesian family of symmetric monoidal Satake categories over finite sets. For the fold I ⊔ I → I its comparison with exterior fusion identifies the resulting product with convolution; the unique map ∅→I carries the coefficient unit to the unit object.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q of characteristic p; G/E is connected reductive.
Λ is a commutative torsion coefficient ring killed by an integer prime to p. The ℓ-adic extension uses a fixed prime ℓ ≠ p and compatible reductions through the imported coefficient adapter.
Satake objects have bounded support, are universally locally acyclic over the leg base, and are flat perverse; representation objects have finite projective coefficient modules.
proofSteps: Use the diagonal base-change square and its closed Grassmannian immersion to define pull-push, check loop equivariance and descend to the Satake categories. Directly check compositional base change; do not replace this diagram by a closed immersion of quotient Hecke stacks.

Compare exterior fusion followed by collision with fusion of the collided blocks, first where the distinct surviving target blocks are disjoint. Within each collapsed block use the chain-composition/base-change and associativity diagrams from GS2; do not restrict the source to the pairwise-distinct locus, whose pullback along a genuine collision is empty.
Every coherence diagram reduces to the same disjoint-locus permutation/composition identity; include empty fibres with the unit. Use the imported operadic language to package these comparisons.
acceptance: Three legs colliding successively agree with their single simultaneous collision.
Permutation inverse/identity comparisons are inverse, and inserting then forgetting a unit leg is identity.
The two paths for I→J→K→L agree after the functor associator; the block-sum comparison uses α ⊔ β, rather than an unrelated map with the same cardinalities.

sources.locator: VI.9 pp226–227, including the footnote p227; Proposition VI.9.4 pp228–229
sources.match: The diagonal pull-push defines arbitrary finite-set maps; the exterior fusion comparison and its symmetry/coherence follow from VI.9.3–VI.9.4.

nodes.title: Weil realization of total cohomology
nodes.statement: For every finite I, finite-projective Λ-local systems on (Div¹)^I are equivalent to continuous finite-projective Λ-representations of W_E^I. Under this equivalence F^I=⊕_r H^r Rπ_* (after pullback to Gr) is exact, faithful and conservative. A map f in Satake has a kernel if ker F^I(f) is a direct summand of F^I(A), and similarly for cokernels; no general abelian or semisimple assertion is made. F^I is strong symmetric monoidal for corrected fusion. For α:I→J, F^J α_! ≅ Res_{dα} F^I, where dα:W_E^J→W_E^I sends (w_j) to (w_{α(i)}); these comparisons respect identities, composition, permutations, exterior products and units. The Drinfeld equivalence applies to locally constant perfect complexes, not all étale complexes.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q of characteristic p; G/E is connected reductive.
Λ is a commutative torsion coefficient ring killed by an integer prime to p. The ℓ-adic extension uses a fixed prime ℓ ≠ p and compatible reductions through the imported coefficient adapter.
Satake objects have bounded support, are universally locally acyclic over the leg base, and are flat perverse; representation objects have finite projective coefficient modules.

The torsion coefficient ring is discrete, killed by an integer prime to p; continuity is for the Weil topology and the discrete module topology. An ℓ-adic version requires compatible reductions and complete coefficient modules, not an arbitrary topologized Representation abbreviation.
proofSteps: Import IV.7.3 in its DLc form. Restrict to finite-projective local systems in degree zero to obtain VI.9.2.
Apply VI.7.10 to the total cohomology functor and VI.9.4 to tensor comparison; cohomological grading is forgotten only after its parity sign is accounted for.

For α:I→J compare the divisor diagonal with B(dα); pullback of representations is restriction in the displayed direction. Use the naturality in IV.7.3 and the cohomological collision square in VI.9 pp226–227.

Fix the Tate stalk convention separately from the parameter cocycle: arithmetic Frobenius acts on Λ(1) by q and geometric Frobenius by q⁻¹. VI.11 pp235–236,239 identifies the P¹ root line Hom(H²,H⁰)=Λ(1). No square root of q enters unnormalized fusion; choosing s²=q gives geometric half-Tate stalk scalar s⁻¹, while the positive-power formula in IX.7.1 pp334–335 concerns parameter untwisting. A formal transport adapter remains a named supplier obligation.
acceptance: For I=∅ the target is finite projective Λ-modules.
For singleton I the action is the local Weil action, and for multiple legs the source is W_E^I, not its diagonal copy.
For α:{1,2}→{*}, dα is the diagonal W_E→W_E²; for an inclusion {1}→{1,2}, dα is projection W_E²→W_E. These directions agree with collision and insertion.
H⁰(P¹)=Λ, H²(P¹)=Λ(−1), hence the root line Hom(H²,H⁰) has geometric scalar q⁻¹; the positive-power parameter normalization is not this stalk action.

sources.locator: Proposition VI.9.2 p226; Proposition IV.7.3 pp165–166 (full faithfulness begins p164)
sources.match: Combines the exact DLc Drinfeld equivalence with the finite-projective degree-zero specialization.
Exactness and split kernel/cokernel criterion; collision square and Weil restriction direction; root-line Tate convention and distinct parameter normalization.

nodes.title: Symmetric constant terms
nodes.statement: For a parabolic P with Levi M, CT_P[deg_P]:Sat^I_G(Λ)→Sat^I_M(Λ) is symmetric monoidal for corrected fusion, commutes with F^I, and is transitive for nested parabolics with the sum of the degree shifts. It respects arbitrary finite-set collision functors, disjoint unions and permutations, with identity, composition and transitivity coherences. The degree is componentwise ⟨2ρ_G−2ρ_M,μ⟩; omission of it changes the weight degrees.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q of characteristic p; G/E is connected reductive.
Λ is a commutative torsion coefficient ring killed by an integer prime to p. The ℓ-adic extension uses a fixed prime ℓ ≠ p and compatible reductions through the imported coefficient adapter.
Satake objects have bounded support, are universally locally acyclic over the leg base, and are flat perverse; representation objects have finite projective coefficient modules.
proofSteps: Use VI.7.13 for landing, degrees and transitivity. Off the collision diagonals the assertion is Künneth and blockwise hyperbolic localization.
Use full faithfulness to extend the comparisons and all their equations. Cohomology-degree parity ensures the modified symmetry matches on G and M.
acceptance: For P=G the functor is identity.
For T⊂M⊂G the two-step weight functor agrees with the direct one with its summed degree shift.
On each component the shifts for G→M→M′ sum to ⟨2ρ_G−2ρ_M′,μ⟩. The shift is integral; neither a half-Tate choice nor an unshifted functor replaces it.
The collision/constant-term square commutes for a fold and an injection, with compatibility between this square and nested-parabolic composition.

sources.locator: Proposition VI.9.6 p230; Proposition VI.7.13 pp223–224; VI.11 p236
sources.match: Shifted constant terms are symmetric monoidal, commute with the fibre functor and exterior fusion, and retain nested-parabolic transitivity. This is the Fargues–Fontaine statement, independent of the rational Witt comparison.

nodes.title: Fusion and Verdier duality
nodes.statement: The inversion/reversal sw* is symmetric monoidal for fusion and F^I sw* ≅ F^I. Verdier duality D is a contravariant symmetric monoidal involution, D sw* ≅ sw* D and F^I D ≅ (F^I)^∨. The internal tensor dual of A is sw*D(A). These identifications retain their evaluation, coevaluation and finite-set coherence data; sw* itself need not be identity.
hypotheses: E is a nonarchimedean local field with residue field F_q of characteristic p; G/E is connected reductive.
Λ is a commutative torsion coefficient ring killed by an integer prime to p. The ℓ-adic extension uses a fixed prime ℓ ≠ p and compatible reductions through the imported coefficient adapter.
Satake objects have bounded support, are universally locally acyclic over the leg base, and are flat perverse; representation objects have finite projective coefficient modules.
proofSteps: VI.8.2 supplies convolution duals before fusion; VI.7.12 supplies F(D A)=F(A)^∨.
VI.9.4 promotes them through the canonical convolution/fusion comparison. F(sw*A)=F(A) and full faithfulness yield the symmetric involution and its duality coherences.
acceptance: A torus weight μ is inverted by sw* and internal dual, with the corresponding dual local system.
The PGL2 minuscule case distinguishes a symmetric Verdier pairing from the alternating SL2 pairing used in VI.12.
Both evaluation/coevaluation triangle identities commute with the convolution-to-fusion comparison and finite-set transport. A fibre-duality isomorphism alone does not specify the internal dual.
For a torus, sw* sends weight μ to −μ while D preserves the support weight and dualizes its local system; sw*D therefore sends (μ,L) to (−μ,L∨).

sources.match: States the fibre-dual comparison and derives the symmetric involutions from existing rigidity.

requests.need: IV.7.3 equivalence D_Lc(X×BW_E^I,Λ) ≅ D_Lc(X×(Div¹)^I,Λ) for locally constant perfect complexes, with degree-zero finite-projective specialization; positive-codimension partial-diagonal purity; ULA/hyperbolic-localization base change. Preserve the distinction from all D_et and explicitly identify the transported Tate character and its stalk/parameter action convention.

Import the existing local Weil group, its topology with open profinite inertia and arithmetic degree. Expose continuous finite-projective product representations, geometric degree = minus arithmetic degree, and the cyclotomic/Tate stalk convention. Do not reconstruct the Weil group here; the current roadmap fixes arithmetic Frobenius as positive degree.

Expose the integral root/coroot pairing, simple coroot basis, 2ρ and component/coroot quotient for a connected reductive group, étale-locally and compatibly with Levi restriction. Pairing 2ρ with every simple coroot is 2; pairing 2ρ_G−2ρ_M is the constant-term component shift. This uses the existing ReductiveGroups root-system development; no dual-group reconstruction or rank-one recognition is requested in this stage.

Use the existing adic/ordinary/solid coefficient comparisons to transport bounded ULA flat-perverse Satake objects and finite-projective fibre local systems through compatible ℓ-power reductions, preserving convolution, proper/base-change comparisons, duality and finite-set transport. State the allowed complete coefficient rings and boundedness hypotheses explicitly; do not identify lisse-site categories with locally constant perfect complexes or define rational completion by an unrestricted tensor with Q_ℓ. VS1 retains the IV.7.3 geometric equivalence.

gaps.title: Formal geometric carriers absent at the pins
gaps.detail: Div¹ v-stacks, local Hecke/Grassmannian diamonds, bounded ULA flat-perverse Satake categories and continuous finite-projective Weil representation categories are supplied by the named earlier owners, not present as Lean carriers at the pins. The suggested file only states genuine light locus/parity/leg-map interfaces on existing types. Heavy targets and all their hypotheses stay in the reader; there are no arbitrary-category stand-ins or admitted data definitions.

gaps.title: Drinfeld transport and coefficient convention adapter
gaps.detail: VS1 does not yet isolate the exact IV.7.3 locally constant perfect equivalence with its finite-projective heart, finite-product and diagonal naturality, transported Tate stalk action and compatible ℓ-adic reductions. The source-level contract and Frobenius signs are fixed here, but its formal carrier-level construction remains with VS1 and the existing ClassFieldTheory Weil owner; VS3 supplies the compatible adic coefficient comparisons with their actual boundedness and coefficient-ring hypotheses. Fusion itself needs no half-Tate choice.

restructure.detail: RT-AREA-geomlanglands/1: the atlas edge GS3:fusion→GS2:Satake-closure conflicts with FS VI8 preceding VI9 and would make imported rigidity cyclic.
restructure.proposal: Remove GS3:fusion as a prerequisite of GS2:Satake-closure; rename its title from Closure after fusion to Convolution closure and rigidity. Add GS2:Satake-closure→GS3:fusion. Preserve the independent VI8 two-leg degeneration proof, which does not use the constructed VI9 fusion tensor.

upstreamNotes.detail: Read current Layer 9: its Weil degree is arithmetic. Import this construction, use its negative for geometric degree, and expose the product continuous-representation/Tate convention adapter rather than rebuilding local Weil theory.
